messages:
jessica.cs: FYI onboarding ticket from NovaPay — they reported rewrap/unwrap failures during BYOK bring-your-own-key setup. errors look like 403s and audit logs on their side don't show any key activity. details pasted below.

jessica.cs: customer env: Azure Key Vault (managed HSM behind PrivateLink), Redwood service principal created, rotation window scheduled tonight 02:00 UTC. they said our rewrap call returns: 
```
HTTP 403 Forbidden
{"error":"Key operation failed: unwrapKey - Access denied to key 'rk-novapay-main' (version mismatch?)"}
```

kevin.eng: thanks — two quick things to confirm: 1) are they using RBAC or legacy access policies on the vault? 2) did they grant the service principal the crypto key role at the key scope (not just vault)? :eyes:

jessica.cs: they said "RBAC is enabled" and they assigned a role called "Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User" to spn `redwood-novapay-sp` at the vault resource level.

dmitri.sec: RBAC level assignments can be scoped. For rewrap/unwrap we need the principal to have the crypto action role at the key resource itself (scope: /.../keys/<key-name>/versions/<version> or the key resource). Also ensure the principal has `Microsoft.KeyVault/managedHsm/keys/decrypt/action` and `wrapKey`/`unwrapKey` HSM permissions.

anita.sre: also PrivateLink can hide diagnostic emission endpoints — if diagnostic settings aren't configured to the storage/LA workspace the Key Vault audit won't show calls. ask them to enable KeyVaultAuditLogs (diagnostic) and send to storage/Log Analytics for the time window.

kevin.eng: possible gotcha — rotation script may be hitting a different key version id than the one the customer allowed. If they provisioned a new version and our envelope references the old version, Key Vault will 404 or give permission-style errors. ask them to run `az keyvault key list-versions --vault-name my-kv --name rk-novapay-main` and paste recent versions.

jessica.cs: passing checklist to customer now: 1) confirm RBAC is enabled, 2) run versions list, 3) add role at key scope if missing, 4) enable diagnostic logs for KeyVaultAuditLogs.

customer note (via jessica.cs): they pasted partial az output showing two versions. I'll attach full blob when they send.

dmitri.sec: follow-ups: - If they used an Azure-managed identity attached to a VM, ensure the identity they're using matches the SPN in our config. - For Managed HSM vs Vault differences: managed HSM enforces AAD principal permission model; you need to add the principal as a crypto user specifically for key ops.

kevin.eng: if that doesn't resolve, ask them to capture the Key Vault diagnostic log entry id and the Azure Activity log for the timeframe and share. We can triage whether the calls reached Key Vault and whether they were dropped by AAD or blocked at HSM.

anita.sre: operational note — do NOT rotate the key until we confirm permissions. If the rotation job runs while permissions are misconfigured we may create a new envelope that nobody can unwrap. Schedule hold: we'll put a temporary freeze on automated rotation for NovaPay until they confirm. :hand:

jessica.cs: done — told customer to pause their rotation and hold the maintenance window. they acknowledged.

deploy-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0412-NOVAPAY-KMS (priority P2) — assigned to kevin.eng + dmitri.sec. Automations: snapshot of current rewrap attempt payloads attached.

kevin.eng: will try repro in staging with a managed HSM replica. if we reproduce, we may need a small SDK change to include explicit key version when performing rewrap. I'll post findings here.

dmitri.sec: also asked security to validate whether customer-level audit retention is sufficient. if diagnostics were off during the failed calls we need to rely on our service-side logs to prove we attempted wrap/unwrap for SLA/incident reasons.

jessica.cs: customer followed up with a couple of extra clues: they saw `EncryptionContext` present in our rewrap payload. they mentioned they thought Azure wouldn't validate encryption context the same way AWS KMS does — could that cause an issue?

kevin.eng: good catch — AWS KMS uses encryptionContext binding that can cause ReEncrypt to fail if context mismatches. Azure managed HSM doesn't enforce an `encryptionContext` field in the same way, but passing extra AAD or malformed fields could cause the HSM SDK to reject the request if the shape differs from what's expected. we'll sanitize the rewrap payload in staging.

anita.sre: next actions (short): 1) kevin to repro + sanitize payload, 2) customer to add principal at key scope + enable diagnostics, 3) dmitri to validate roles required and prepare guidance snippet for their runbook, 4) jessica to keep customer on hold for rotation. ETA: 4 hours.

jessica.cs: customer agreed to make the RBAC change and enable diagnostics; will update when completed. :thumbsup:
